[b][size=xx-large][color=#ffffff][u]Hack Forum News - Edition 27[/u][/color][/size][/b]

[b]Welcome back to the Hack Forum News. Where we keep you up to date on the weekly events and news happening on site and around the world. If you have never heard of the Hack Forum News, don't worry, we have you covered. We are a team of members from the Hack Forums community who are journalists and writers, and we are here to keep you in the loop of the changes around the site and the events happening around the world.[/b]

[hr]

[img]https://hackforums.net/images/hfnews/headlines-red.png[/img]
[size=medium][b]Writer -[/b][/size] [mention=2331053]

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6314337][color=#ffffff]The Hack Forums Wiki Returns[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=2331053]

The Hack Forums Wiki is back in action and is now under way to a few big changes. The site has been under some work recently as the site was sadly left with a load of issues and no one was running the official site. Thanks to everyone within the HF news team, the site is now under new leadership and, thanks to [mention=1] allowing the team to start their work on this while maintaining the HF news, the site is back getting some lovely changes and getting updated daily to bring it back to a new modern day Wikipedia with a load of information for everyone to read up on.

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6299866][color=#ffffff]Hack Forums News Team - Become a Writer[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=2331053]

Are you looking to join the HF news team? Do you enjoy making threads or even want to become a better writer? Well, we are looking for members of the site to help write each week and are looking for anyone who has any interest. We have a few new sections opening up right now, and we would love for you to see if they would be anything of interest to you. If you are interested, please check out the thread or contact [mention=2331053] to discuss joining the team behind the HF News.

[size=xx-large][color=#00D9FF]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6315624]ChatGPT getting dumber?[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=5699666] [/b][/color][/size]

A thoughtful thread that taps into a feeling many users quietly share. [mention=5699666] breaks down how ChatGPT used to feel sharper, more helpful, and less restrictive - especially for coding, cybersecurity questions, and product comparisons - and contrasts that with recent experiences of refusals, misunderstandings, and weaker outputs. The discussion touches on safety filters, model changes, and whether tools like Perplexity are starting to feel more reliable. [i]A great read if you've ever caught yourself thinking, "Wasn't this better before?"[/i]

[hr]

[size=xx-large][color=#00FF88]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6315696]How old were you when you began using a computer?[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=4402880] [/b][/color][/size]

A simple question that unlocked a surprisingly nostalgic discussion. Members share their first memories with computers. [i]It's one of those threads that reminds you just how diverse the HF user base is, while also highlighting how fast technology became central to everyone's lives.[/i]

[hr]

[size=xx-large][color=#FF6B00]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6315692]Office24 ProPlus2024 serial[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=5458992] [/b][/color][/size]

Another helpful thread that shows what HF community is all about. Sharing a key might seem a simple move, but it might make a big difference to someone who needs it. [i]I really hope we see more of this![/i]

[hr]

[size=xx-large][color=#FF00FF]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6315850][Legends] Brute force AI tool that tries really hard to behave like a human user[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=5568595] [/b][/color][/size]

An eye-opening post that dives into BruteForceAI - a tool that blends brute forcing with LLM-driven behavior to mimic real users. From DOM analysis and adaptive retries to human-like delays and jitter, this isn't your old-school attack script. The thread doesn't glorify it, but it does raise important awareness for anyone in red team, blue team, or defensive security. [i]One of those posts that quietly signals a shift in how AI is being weaponized.[/i]

[hr]

[size=xx-large][color=#FFD700]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6315845][EDUCATIONAL] Predicting RNG Output via Reverse Engineering[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=5699666] [/b][/color][/size]

A solid educational share focusing on why weak pseudorandom number generators can be dangerous. The linked video walks through reversing common PRNGs, reconstructing internal state from outputs, and real-world demos tied to games and applications. Perfect for beginners interested in reverse engineering, algorithm behavior, and security fundamentals - and [i]a good reminder that "random" often isn't as random as people think.[/i]

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]Taiwan opens new cloud centre to bolster sovereign AI hardware development[/color][/size][/b][/u]  
Taiwan inaugurated a new cloud computing centre in Tainan powered by 15 megawatts of infrastructure, including Nvidia H200 and Blackwell chips, strengthening its AI and hardware ecosystem.  
[b][url=https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/taiwan-opens-new-cloud-centre-bolster-sovereign-ai-effort-2025-12-12/]Source[/url][/b]

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]First monolithic 3D chip built in US foundry delivers AI performance gains[/color][/size][/b][/u]  
Researchers announced the first monolithic 3D chip manufactured in a US foundry, offering much higher wiring density and significant speed improvements for AI workloads.  
[b][url=https://techxplore.com/news/2025-12-monolithic-3d-chip-built-foundry.html]Source[/url][/b]

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]Photonic memory latch prototype could enable optical processor caches at 60 GHz[/color][/size][/b][/u]  
Researchers developed a prototype photonic memory latch that could let optical processor caches operate up to 60 GHz, about 20 times faster than conventional electronic caches.  
[b][url=https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/usc-and-us-madison-researchers-debut-foundry-made-photonic-memory-latch]Source[/url][/b]

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]Dell plans PC price increase amid AI hardware and memory shortages[/color][/size][/b][/u]  
Dell Technologies is reportedly preparing to raise PC prices due to ongoing memory chip shortages and rising costs driven by AI infrastructure demand.  
[b][url=https://www.webpronews.com/dell-to-hike-pc-prices-5-20-amid-ai-driven-chip-shortages/]Source[/url][/b]

[u][b][size=large][color=#ffffff]Chinese government lists local AI hardware suppliers excluding Nvidia for public contracts[/color][/size][/b][/u]  
China compiled a list of government-approved AI hardware suppliers that currently includes local firms such as Cambricon and Huawei but does not include Nvidia, reflecting local industrial priorities.  
[b][url=https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/china-starts-list-of-government-approved-ai-hardware-suppliers-cambricon-and-huawei-are-in-nvidia-is-not]Source[/url][/b]
